F-132 CHROME: 555 + 556 + 557 done -- THE SPEC 5.1 GROUP IS COMPLETE AND SHIPPED IN ORDER. REMAINING: US-558 (S, solid overlays) and US-559 (M, local sync stamp). Both are independent of the group and of each other -- take either. NEXT ITERATION: US-558 (smaller, and US-559 has the ONE-12-HOUR-RULE constraint worth a fresh context). ***

*** US-556 CLOSED passes:true -- kebab visual box vs hit box + the .menu-head fix. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

**THE STALE NUMBER IN AN AC IS NOT ALWAYS THE WHOLE AC -- RE-DERIVE AND THE PREMISE MAY SPLIT.** I was warned AC-1's "28px bar" was stale. Re-reading it against 34 did not just update a number: it revealed the AC described TWO defects and US-557 had already cured ONE of them. --fs-primary is 34 and --bar-h is now 34, so the GLYPH exactly fills the band; only the 40px BOX still overflows. I found it because a negative self-test I wrote went RED on an assertion I expected to pass, and I re-read the assertion instead of deleting it. **Generalise: when a self-test fails in the direction you did not predict, the model is usually right and your restatement of the story is wrong.**

**"EXACTLY FLUSH" IS NOT "SAFELY INSIDE".** A 34px line box in a 34px band has zero margin, and glyph INK is not bound by a `line-height: 1` box. So the glyph half still deserved fixing even though the strict inequality no longer failed. Assert `<` not `<=` when the quantity is a paint bound.

**DERIVE THE SIGNED SHORTFALL INSTEAD OF LANDING TWO LITERALS.** Iris specced `inset: -6px -7px` -- correct arithmetic for a 28px box, wrong for the 34px one. `inset: calc((var(--bar-h) - var(--tap-min)) / 2)` is HALF THE SIGNED SHORTFALL: negative while the band is under the minimum (grows the target by exactly the missing px, hit box == --tap-min), positive if the band ever exceeds it (pseudo shrinks inside, button already over the minimum). Self-correcting BOTH ways. **When a spec hands you two magnitudes, ask what they are the difference between -- the subtraction usually belongs in the sheet.**

**AUDIT BY WHAT A CONTROL PAINTS, NOT BY THE BOX IT RESERVES.** I nearly modelled AC-4 as "no control's box exceeds its band" -- which would have flagged `.dot` (a 40px box in a 16px band) as a fourth defect. `.dot` is CORRECT: its box is transparent + border-less and its mark is an 8px `::before`. That is the precedent my whole fix rests on, and it was already in the sheet. **Check whether the sheet already solved your problem before inventing a mechanism; then pin the precedent, so a later change to it invalidates your citation loudly.**

**THE SAME DEFECT CAN HAVE OPPOSITE CORRECT FIXES.** #menu-btn shrinks to its band; `.menu-head` GROWS to its control. Not inconsistency -- #topbar defends a 320px stage budget US-557 just fought for, an overlay head defends nothing. **Ask what the band costs before deciding which side moves.**

**A PASSING TEST CAN STILL BE A STALE MEASUREMENT.** US-555's bar-width model charged the kebab at `--tap-min`. After my change it charges 40 for a 34px box -- green, and wrong, and an OVER-estimate so it would never have gone red. Moved the pin to read the declared width, and made the helper ASSERT the declaration is a `var()` (a bare literal would give a plausible number and re-create the drift). **Green is not evidence a model still measures its subject.**

**`position: relative` IS THE QUIET FAILURE ON ANY ::after HIT-AREA.** Without it the pseudo anchors to the nearest positioned ancestor -- here #topbar, which is `position: fixed` -- and the hit area lands somewhere else while every other assertion passes. It needs its own test, because nothing else in the file can see it.

**READ THE PRIOR STORY'S PM FLAG BEFORE BUILDING, THEN SAY WHY IT DOES OR DOESN'T BITE.** US-560 flagged that the kiosk renders at 1280x720, which could invalidate canvas-budgeted chrome work. It does not bite US-556 -- every claim here is a RATIO inside the uniformly-scaled 480x320 #stage, so it holds at any output mode and BL-034 cannot invalidate it. Saying that explicitly is much stronger than not mentioning it.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed): PowerShell tool does NOT support heredocs for python -- Write a temp .py and run it, then delete it. `git commit -m @'...'@` (single-quoted here-string, closing delimiter at column 0) DOES work in the PowerShell tool. **pytest prints NO summary line in this repo's config** -- `-q` gives dots only, so gate on `$LASTEXITCODE` plus "zero F/E characters in the progress output", not on a "N passed" string. tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 888 tests, ~4-5 min -- run it FOREGROUND (TD-059). A `PostToolUse` security hook flags `eval()` in new files; an `ast.parse` + whitelisted-node walk is ~15 lines and avoids it entirely. Index lock CLEAR all session.
